verses.sanskrit: भीष्म उवाच। एवमुक्तो मतङ्गस्तु संशितात्मा यतव्रतः । सहस्रमेकपादेन ततो ध्याने व्यतिष्ठत ॥१॥
verses.english: Bhishma said Thus addressed by Indra, Matanga refused to hear what he was commanded. On the other hand, with regulated vows and purified soul, he practised austerer penances by standing on one foot for a thousand years, being deeply engaged in Yoga-meditation.

verses.sanskrit: तं सहस्रावरे काले शक्रो द्रष्टुमुपागमत् । तदेव च पुनर्वाक्यमुवाच बलवृत्रहा ॥२॥
verses.english: After a thousand years had passed away, Shakra once more came to see him. Indeed the destroyer of Vala and Vritra laid to him the same words.

verses.sanskrit: मतङ्ग उवाच । इदं वर्षसहस्रं वै ब्रह्मचारी समाहितः । अतिष्ठमेकपादेन ब्राह्मण्यं नाप्नुयां कथम् ॥३॥
verses.english: Matanga said I have passed these thousand years, standing on one foot, with soul engaged in meditation and in the observance of the vow of celibacy. Why is it that I have not yet succeeded in acquiring the dignity of a Brahmana?

verses.sanskrit: शक्र उवाच। चण्डालयोनौ जातेन नावाप्यं वै कथञ्चन । अन्यं कामं वृणीष्व त्वं मा वृथा तेऽस्त्वयं श्रमः ॥४॥
verses.english: Shakra said One born as a Chandala cannot, by any means, acquire the dignity of a Brahmana. Do you, therefore, name some other boon so that all this labour of yours may not prove futile! Thus addressed by the king of the celestials, Matanga became filled with grief. He went to Gaya, and passed there a century of years, standing all the while on one foot.

verses.sanskrit: एवमुक्तो मतङ्गस्तु भृशं शोकपरायणः । अध्यतिष्ठद्गयां गत्वा सौङ्गुष्ठेन शतं समाः ॥५॥
सुदुर्वहं वहन्योगं कृशो धमनिसन्ततः । त्वगस्थिभूतो धर्मात्मा स पपातेति नः श्रुतम् ॥६॥
verses.english: On account of the observance of such Yoga which was extremely difficult to bear, he became very much emaciated and his arteries and veins became swollen and visible. He was reduced to only skin and bones. We have heard that righteous person, while practising those austerities at Gaya, dropped down on the ground from sheer exhaustion.

verses.sanskrit: त पतन्तमभिद्रुत्य परिजग्राह वासवः । वराणामीश्वरो दाता सर्वभूतहिते रतः ॥७॥
verses.english: Seeing him falling down the lord and giver of boons, engaged in the behoof of all creatures viz., Vasava, speedily came to that spot and held him fast.

verses.sanskrit: शक्र उवाच। मतङ्ग ब्राह्मणत्वं ते विरुद्धमिह दृश्यते । ब्राह्मण्यं दुर्लभतरं संवृतं परिपन्थिभिः ॥८॥
verses.english: Shakra said It seems, O Matanga , that the dignity of a Brahmana which you seek is illsuited to you. That dignity is incapable of being acquired by you. Indeed in your case, it is beset with many dangers.

verses.sanskrit: पूजयन्सुखमाप्नोति दुःखमाप्नोत्यपूजयन् । ब्राह्मणः सर्वभूतानां योगक्षेमसमर्पिता ॥९॥
verses.english: A person by adoring a Brahmana acquires happiness; while by abstaining from such worship, he gets grief and misery. The Brahmana is as regards all creatures, the giver of what they prize or covet and the protector of what they already have.

verses.sanskrit: ब्राह्मणेभ्योऽनुतृप्यन्ते पितरो देवतास्तथा । ब्राह्मणः सर्वभूतानां मतङ्ग पर उच्यते ॥१०॥
verses.english: It is through the Brahmanas that the departed manes and the deities become pleased. The Brahmana, O Matanga, is said to be the foremost of all created Beings. The Brahmana grants all objects which are desired and in the way they are desired.

verses.sanskrit: ब्राह्मणः कुरुते तद्धि यथा यद्यच्च वाञ्छति । बह्वीस्तु संविशन्त्योनीर्जायमानः पुनःपुनः ॥११॥
verses.english: Passing through numberless orders of being and undergoing repeated rebirths, one succeeds in some subsequent birth in acquiring the dignity of a Brahmana.

verses.sanskrit: पर्याये तात कस्मिंश्चिद्ब्राह्मण्यमिह विन्दति । तदुत्सृज्येह दुष्प्रापं ब्राह्मण्यमकृतात्मभिः ॥१२॥
verses.english: That dignity is really incapable of being obtained by persons of impure souls. Do you, therefore, relinquish the idea Do you name some other boon. The particular boon which you seek is incapable of being granted to you.

verses.sanskrit: अन्यं वरं वृणीष्व त्वं दुर्लभोऽयं हि ते वरः । मतङ्ग उवाच । किं मां तुदसि दुःखार्तं मृतं मारयसे च मां ॥१३॥
verses.english: Matanga said Stricken as I am with grief, why, O Shakra, do you afflict me further? You are striking one that is already dead, by this conduct. I do not pity you who having acquired the dignity of a Brahmana fail to retain it.

verses.sanskrit: त्वां तु शोचामि यो लब्ध्वा ब्राह्मण्यं न बुभूषसे । ब्राह्मण्यं यदि दुष्प्रापं त्रिभिर्वर्णैः शतक्रतो ॥१४॥
verses.english: Those who having won the dignity of a Brahmana that, like wealth, is so difficult to acquire, do not seek to keep it up, must be considered as the most wretched in this world. Indeed, they are the most sinful of all creatures.

verses.sanskrit: सुदुर्लभं सदाऽवाप्य नानुतिष्ठन्ति मानवाः । यः पापेभ्यः पापतमस्तेषामधम एव सः ॥१५॥
ब्राह्मण्यं यो न जानीते धनं लब्ध्वेव दुर्लभम् । दुष्प्रापं खलु विप्रत्वं प्राप्तं दुरनुपालनम् ॥१६॥
verses.english: Forsooth, the dignity of a Brahmana is highly difficult to attain, and being attained, is difficult to maintain, it is capable of removing every sort of grief. Alas, having got it men do not always seek to keep it up.

verses.sanskrit: दुरावापमवाप्यैतन्नानुतिष्ठन्ति मानवाः । एकारामो ह्यहं शक्र निर्द्वन्द्वो निष्परिग्रहः ॥१७॥
verses.english: When even such persons are considered as Brahmanas, why is it that I, who am pleased with my own self, who am superior to all pairs of opposites, who am dissociated from all worldly objects, who am observant of the duty of mercy towards all creatures and of selfcontrol of conduct, should be considered worthy of that dignity?

verses.sanskrit: अहिंसादममास्थाय कथं नार्हामि विप्रताम् । दैवं तु कथमेतद्वै यदहं मातृदोषतः ॥१८॥
verses.english: not How unfortunate I am, O Purandara, that through the sin of my mother I have been reduced to this plight, although I am not unrighteous in my conduct?

verses.sanskrit: एतामवस्थां संप्राप्तो धर्मज्ञः सन्पुरन्दर । नूनं दैवं न शक्यं हि पौरुषेणातिवर्तितुम् ॥१९॥
verses.english: Forsooth, Destiny is incapable of being warded off or conquered by individual exertion since, O lord, I am unable to acquire, despite these.persistent attempts of mine the object for the acquisi.ion of which I am trying.

verses.sanskrit: यदर्थं यत्नवानेव न लभे विप्रतां विभो । एवंगते तु धर्मज्ञ दातुमर्हसि मे वरम् ॥२०॥
verses.english: When such is the case, O righteous one, you should grant me some other boon if, indeed, I have become worthy of your favour or if I have a little of merit!

verses.sanskrit: यदि तेऽहमनुग्राह्यः किञ्चिद्वा सुकृतं मम । वैशम्पायन उवाच। वृणीष्वेति तदा प्राह ततस्तं बलवृत्रहा ॥२१॥
verses.english: Bhishma said The destroyer of Vala and Vritra then said to him Do you name the boon! Thus urged by the great Indra, Matanga said the following words

verses.sanskrit: चोदितस्तु महेन्द्रेण मतङ्गः प्राब्रवीदिदम् । यथा कामविहारी स्यां कामरूपी विहङ्गमः ॥२२॥
verses.english: Matanga said Gifted with the power of assuming any form at will, let me be able to journey through the skies and let me enjoy whatever pleasures I may wish for. And let me also have the willing worship of both Brahmanas and Kshatriyas.

verses.sanskrit: ब्रह्मक्षत्राविरोधेन पूजां च प्राप्नुयामहम् । यथा ममाक्षया कीर्तिर्भवेच्चापि पुरन्दर ॥२३॥
verses.english: I bow to you by bending my head, O god! You should do that also by which my fame, O Purandara, may live eternally in the world!

verses.sanskrit: कर्तुमहसि तदेव शिरसा त्वां प्रसादये । शक्र उवाच। छन्दोदेव इति ख्यातः स्त्रीणां पूज्यो भविष्यसि । कीर्तिश्च तेऽतुला वत्स त्रिषु लोकेषु यास्यति ॥२४॥
verses.english: Shakra said You will be celebrated as the deity of a particular measure of verse and you will get the worship of all women. Your fame, O son, shall become peerless in the three worlds.

verses.sanskrit: एवं तस्मै वरं दत्वा वासवोऽन्तरधीयत ॥२५॥
verses.english: Having granted him these boons, Vasava disappeared there and then. Matanga also renouncing his lifebreaths, acquired a high place.

verses.sanskrit: प्राणांस्त्यक्त्वा मतङ्गोऽपि संप्राप्तःस्थानमुत्तमम् । एवमेतत्परं स्थानं ब्राह्मण्यं नाम भारत । तच्च दुष्प्रापमिह वै महेन्द्रवचनं यथा ॥२६॥
verses.english: You may thus see, O Bharata that the dignity of a Brahmana is very high. That dignity is incapable of being acquired here as said by the great Indra himself.
